events.title: Demo update 1.0.6: district routes, calmer early game, junction fixes
events.summary: The demo has a new update, 1.0.6. Steam installs it automatically. Most of it came from your reports, here in the discussions and on Discord. New District routes. With the Info tool, click a district to see the routes of the cars coming to it. Click it again to see the cars leaving it. All other cars turn grey, so you can see where its traffic actually goes. events.title: Where the traffic comes from: how the city grows
events.summary: Every article so far has been about carrying traffic — interchanges, then buses, trains and metro. This one is about where the traffic comes from. In Traffic Architect you don't need to worry about building the city: it grows on its own, and every building it grows is a machine that makes cars. events.title: Buses, trains and metro — taking cars off the roads you built
events.summary: Traffic Architect is a traffic game first. You build the roads, the junctions and the interchanges; the city grows along them and fills them with cars. Public transport is how you take that load back off — and it's the part of the game nobody has seen yet. A bus line is a loop {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46246597/230399318af451ded0f37a67c8413bdcd40ba061.gif Pick a hub, add stops, and buses start running the loop. events.title: Feature spotlight #1: Highways & interchanges - when more lanes aren't enough
events.summary: {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46246597/7b4ee4f087540b377e220dbb6c95365b537ce8a4.gif Every city in Traffic Architect hits this moment: a crossroad that used to work fine is now a parking lot. events.title: Hello, Steam! Traffic Architect has arrived
events.summary: Hello, Steam! Traffic Architect has arrived 🚦 We just passed Steam's review and the store page you're looking at is officially live — this is the very first post in what will become a long devlog series. What is Traffic Architect? A traffic management city builder: the city grows on its own, and your job is the network — roads, junctions, and now entire transit systems — that keeps it moving.
